author: nickaturley
text: This is the positioned that I would have expected center/left to take. And you do see it — in Europe. Merkel isn't arguing that Trump shouldn’t have been banned. She’s arguing that Twitter shouldn’t have had the power to do so. https://t.co/D6l0m0KdEg

author: nickaturley
text: It seems perfectly possible to support Trump's ban without relying on the autonomy of private enterprise as an argument. For instance, one might argue that the state has an obligation to prevent violence inducing speech on social media, and thus should regulate Twitter

author: nickaturley
text: Don’t get me wrong. This line of argument is coherent — whether you agree with it or not. But it’s not an argument  one would expect to see  from the left. Would the same people support a similar ban of left-wing activists who advocate for looting as a political statement?

author: nickaturley
text: It’s not surprising to see folks center/left favor a trump Twitter ban. What IS surprising, however, is the degree to which the justifications seems to lean on the autonomy of private enterprise (“Twitter is a private company and they can ban anyone they want").
I can assure you that my departure from office is going to be very boring.
